headline: Salmon, pork tenderloin, black bean bowls, garlic shrimp pasta and crispy cod bites.

ingredients: 1.5 lb salmon fillets (4 pieces; one is lunch leftovers)
1 large head broccoli, cut into florets (about 4 cups)
1 tsp garlic powder, ½ tsp dried dill, salt and pepper
5 oz arugula, 1 avocado, 2 tbsp lemon vinaigrette (from Sunday)
nights.prep: Broccoli is chopped and quinoa cooked on Sunday. Save the 4th fillet for Tuesday's lunch.
steps: Heat the oven to 425°F and line a sheet pan with foil or parchment paper.
Toss the broccoli with 2 tbsp oil and a pinch of salt on the pan. Roast for 10 minutes.
Meanwhile, pat the salmon dry with paper towels. Rub with 1 tbsp oil, garlic powder, dill and pepper. Lay thin lemon slices on top.
Push the broccoli to the edges and set the salmon in the middle, skin side down. Roast 10–12 minutes, until the fish flakes easily with a fork (145°F).
Warm the quinoa in the microwave for 1–2 minutes with a splash of water.
Toss the arugula with the vinaigrette and top it with sliced avocado.
nights.title: Sheet-pan lemon salmon & broccoli
nights.toddler: About 2 oz flaked salmon (check for bones), 2 tbsp quinoa, soft broccoli "trees" and avocado slices. Skip the peppery arugula and stir a few soft spinach leaves into the quinoa instead.
nights.why: Salmon is the richest common source of heart-protective omega-3s. One pan, 30 minutes.

ingredients: 1 tsp each dried Italian seasoning and garlic powder, salt and pepper
1 bunch kale (or a 5 oz bag), stems removed, chopped
nights.prep: Baby carrots need no prep. Save about ⅓ of the pork for Wednesday or Thursday lunch, and pack extra beans and kale as a side.
steps: Heat the oven to 425°F. Toss the carrots with 1 tbsp oil and a pinch of salt on a sheet pan.
Pat the pork dry. Rub it with 1 tbsp oil, the Italian seasoning, garlic powder, ½ tsp salt and pepper. Set it on the pan next to the carrots.
Roast 20–25 minutes, until a meat thermometer in the thickest part reads 145°F. Rest it on a cutting board for 5 minutes, then slice.
While the pork roasts, warm 2 tbsp oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Add the garlic and cook 1 minute, until fragrant but not brown.
Add the kale and broth. Cover and cook 4–5 minutes until the kale softens.
Stir in the beans and heat 3 minutes. Squeeze in the lemon and season to taste.
nights.technique: Roasting a whole tenderloin to temperature
nights.title: Herb pork tenderloin with garlicky white beans & kale
nights.toddler: Thin pork slices cut into small strips, beans lightly mashed with a fork, soft carrots cut lengthwise, and finely chopped kale mixed into the beans.
nights.why: Pork tenderloin is about as lean as chicken breast, and the beans bring fiber that blunts the glucose rise.

ingredients: 1 tsp cumin, 1 tsp chili powder, ½ tsp garlic powder
2 cups cooked brown rice (from Sunday, or 2 microwave pouches)
½ cup plain Greek yogurt (in place of sour cream)
½ cup shredded cheddar or Mexican-blend cheese
nights.prep: Rice is cooked and romaine washed on Sunday. Extra beans make a great breakfast with scrambled eggs.
steps: Warm the oil in a saucepan over medium heat. Add the beans, corn, spices and ¼ cup water.
Simmer 5–6 minutes, stirring now and then, until the corn is hot. Mash about a quarter of the beans against the pan to thicken.
Reheat the rice in the microwave with a splash of water, covered, 2 minutes.
Mash 1 avocado with half the lime juice and a pinch of salt. Dice the other avocado.
Build bowls: romaine, rice, beans and corn, then avocado, salsa, a spoon of yogurt and a sprinkle of cheese.
nights.title: Black bean & corn burrito bowls
nights.toddler: A scoop of rice with the beans mostly mashed, cheese melted on top, and mashed avocado on the side. Hold the salsa or offer a tiny taste. Mash the corn a little if your toddler is still learning to chew it.
nights.why: Beans plus brown rice make a complete protein with lots of soluble fiber, which helps lower LDL cholesterol. No oven.

ingredients: 12 oz–1 lb frozen raw shrimp, peeled and deveined (thawed)
Optional for adults: pinch of red pepper flakes
nights.prep: Move the shrimp to the fridge Wednesday night. One serving keeps for the next day's lunch.
steps: Thaw the shrimp if needed: put them in a colander under cold running water for about 5 minutes. Pat dry.
Boil a large pot of salted water. Cook the pasta 1 minute less than the package says. Scoop out 1 cup of pasta water, then drain.
While the pasta cooks, heat 2 tbsp oil in a large skillet over medium-high. Add the shrimp in one layer and cook 2 minutes per side, until pink and curled into a "C" shape. Move them to a plate.
Lower the heat to medium. Add 1 tbsp oil, the garlic and tomatoes, and cook 2 minutes.
Add the spinach and a splash of pasta water. Stir until wilted, about 1 minute.
Add the pasta, shrimp, lemon juice and Parmesan. Toss, adding more pasta water until glossy. Sprinkle red pepper flakes on the adult plates only.
nights.technique: Searing shrimp and finishing pasta in the pan
nights.title: Garlic shrimp & spinach pasta
nights.toddler: Shrimp chopped into pea-sized pieces, short pasta pieces, quartered tomatoes, wilted spinach and a little extra Parmesan.
nights.why: Pasta cooked al dente digests more slowly than soft-cooked pasta. Keep adult portions to about 1 cup cooked and let the shrimp and spinach fill the rest of the plate.

ingredients: 1.25 lb cod fillets (frozen is fine, thawed), cut into 1½-inch chunks
1 tsp paprika, ½ tsp garlic powder, ¼ tsp salt
Olive oil spray (or 2 tbsp olive oil)
5 oz arugula, 1 avocado, 2 tbsp lemon vinaigrette
Lemon wedges; optional dip of Greek yogurt mixed with lemon and dill
nights.prep: Move the cod to the fridge Wednesday night. Quinoa is from Sunday. Cod bites are best fresh; leftovers re-crisp in a 400°F oven in 5 minutes.
steps: Heat the oven to 425°F. Set a wire rack on the sheet pan if you have one; otherwise line it with parchment.
Set up 3 shallow bowls: flour in the first; beaten eggs in the second; panko, Parmesan, paprika, garlic powder and salt in the third.
Pat the cod dry. Dip each piece in flour, then egg, then press into the crumbs. Place on the pan.
Spray or drizzle the tops with olive oil. Bake 12–15 minutes, until golden and the fish flakes easily (145°F).
While it bakes, microwave the peas with 2 tbsp water, covered, for 3–4 minutes. Warm the quinoa.
Toss the arugula with vinaigrette and sliced avocado.
nights.title: Crispy baked cod bites with peas & quinoa
nights.toddler: 2–3 cod bites broken into smaller pieces (check for bones), peas lightly mashed, quinoa and avocado. The yogurt dip makes it fun.
nights.why: Homemade fish sticks, baked instead of fried, are a toddler favorite, and cod is very lean.

leftovers.use: Mon dinner, Fri dinner, adult lunch bowls
Tue lunch, flaked over a salad or into the toddler's quinoa
Wed or Thu lunch, sliced into wraps or grain bowls
Lunch, or a side with Wednesday's bowls
Thu breakfast with eggs, or mashed on toast for the toddler
Next-day lunch. Eat within 1 day and reheat until steaming.

steps.text: Rinse 1½ cups quinoa and simmer it in 3 cups water for 15 min, covered, then rest 5 min. Once the pot is free, cook 1 cup brown rice in it (about 40 min), or skip this and use 2 microwave pouches on Wednesday. Cool both and refrigerate separately.
steps.title: Cook the grains

steps.text: Do the spinach, kale and romaine. Store each wrapped in a paper towel inside a bag. Arugula is usually pre-washed; leave it in its container.
steps.title: Wash and dry the greens

steps.text: Cut the broccoli into florets for Monday and store in a container.
steps.title: Chop the vegetables

steps.text: 6 tbsp olive oil, 3 tbsp lemon juice, 1 tsp Dijon mustard, a pinch of salt and pepper. Shake in a jar and refrigerate.
steps.title: Mix the lemon vinaigrette

steps.text: Fresh salmon needs no thawing. Move the cod and shrimp from the freezer to the fridge on Wednesday night.
steps.title: Plan the thaws

prep.storage: Cooked grains keep 4–5 days in the fridge. Cooked meat keeps 3–4 days; shrimp and fish are best within 1–2 days.

shopNote: Best split this week: Jewel-Osco by Tuesday, Nov 3 (salmon $4.99/lb, cod portions, produce) and Aldi (avocados, Parmesan, staples). Mariano's has the cheapest plain pork tenderloin.
toddlerRules: Set aside the toddler's portion before adding salt or red pepper flakes. Cut food into pea-sized pieces, flatten or mash beans and peas, quarter small round foods, and flake fish by hand to check for bones.
